title: 1995 AHSME Problem 17
statement: Given regular pentagon \(ABCDE,\) a circle can be drawn that is tangent to \(\overline{DC}\) at \(D\) and to \(\overline{AB}\) at \(A.\) The number of degrees in minor arc \(\widehat{AD}\) is

solutions.text: Let \(O\) be the circle’s center. The direction changes by \(72^\circ\) at each vertex of the pentagon, so the acute angle between lines \(AB\) and \(DC\) is \(36^\circ.\) The radii to their tangency points are perpendicular to these lines; for the circle shown, the minor central angle \(\angle AOD\) is the supplementary angle \(180^\circ-36^\circ=144^\circ.\) Therefore minor arc \(\widehat{AD}\) measures \(144^\circ,\) and the correct answer is E.
hints: The radii to \(A\) and \(D\) are perpendicular to the tangent sides
Use the \(72^\circ\) exterior angle of a regular pentagon to compare \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{DC}\)
